cards.title: The short answer
items: A clause set decomposes somebody else’s written rules so the miner can be scored against them

Two repositories hold them, split by whether the source rulebook is public: benchmark decompositions can be read by anyone checking a published figure, and anything derived from a private corpus is licensed to nobody
Neither is reachable from the mining side

cards.title: Not shown here
items: The three-region diff and the serving path — the advisor never sees a clause set
Connected but out of scope: Clause checker, Pipeline, Ports, Store, Three-region diff, Annotation store

cards.title: Constraints
items: An answer key is never distributed to anyone — a shipped answer key is a shipped evaluation, and the decompositions are months of judgement rather than code

A contract set ships; an answer key does not — a contract set decomposes what a harness publishes about itself, so it holds for every installation and gives a first run something true to say — same shape, opposite purpose
